claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Premature failure of the Cr coating at elevated temperature is caused by Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The baseline elemental Cr coating protects zirconium-alloy cladding under normal PWR conditions.
A thin Al2O3 interlayer between Cr and the zirconium alloy will inhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The Al2O3 interlayer will not compromise corrosion or oxidation protection in either subcritical PWR water or high-temperature steam.
A tens-of-nanometers Al2O3 interlayer can remain continuous and amorphous at the Cr/Zr-alloy interface.
Al2O3 has sufficiently low atomic diffusivity and ion mobility to function as the proposed interfacial barrier at elevated temperature.
The chemical inertness of Al2O3 contributes to restriction of Cr and Zr transport across the interface.
Suppressing Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent detrimental intermetallic formation or diffusion-induced coating degradation.
The Al2O3 interlayer will still allow the outer Cr layer to form protective Cr2O3.
Protective Cr2O3 formation will be retained during both normal-water operation and accident-relevant steam exposure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Al2O3-containing coating will show significantly reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Al2O3-containing coating will exhibit delayed coating failure.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the Al2O3-containing coating will maintain oxidation and corrosion protection during moderate-temperature and transient high-temperature exposures.
The interlayer is expected to remain effective at standard PWR operating temperatures and during short-to-moderate steam exposures at approximately 800–1200 °C.
Multi-component alloy barriers can suppress interdiffusion and increase diffusion-barrier failure temperature.
